content.text:
Not directly showing 351.802(a)(2) text. Not crucial. The submission's Q2(d) claim about "her own notice must state her three most recent ratings (351.802(a)(2))" is plausible and not a credit criterion. No fab.

Now let's think about Q1_fab: "2026-17335 ... It also conforms the part 351 authority citation to the appeals rule (adds 5 U.S.C. 1103 and 1104)". Key says correction adds 1103 and 1104. Fine. "amendatory instructions 15, 36 and 39" — can't verify quickly; likely accurate. Not obviously fabricated.

Also Q1(e): "2026-21316 ... amends 351.203 (definition of 'Rating of record'...). The authority citation 'continues to read' as already amended." Key says 21316 revises the definition of "rating of record" in 351.203 and 351.503(a)(1), (b)(2), (b)(3). The submission only mentions 351.203, which the criterion allows ("and/or 351.503"). Fine.

Q1(e) requires listing every other final rule with effect on or after the main rule's effective date. The submission lists the three. Good.

Now Q5 fab: example dates 1996/2021 — confirmed at 91 FR 49186: Employee A SCD 1996, 3/3/3 +12 → 1984; Employee B 2021, 5/5/5 +20 → 2001. The submission said "Employee A 3/3/3, 1996 SCD, outranks Employee B 5/5/5, 2021 SCD" — accurate. Good.

Note also the submission's Q5(a)(i) arithmetic: Lee SCD 1998 minus 12 = 1986; Park 2019 minus 20 = 1999. Key says the same. Good.

Now Q8: The submission says the 12-week statement at 91 FR 65926 — key says 65927. Both possible; the grep shows 65926 lines 303-305 exactly that sentence. So the submission is accurate; the key's 65927 is for a different passage.

Q8(b) also says "The new 630.1403(a)(3) says administrative leave is generally for brief periods (usually not more than 1 workday)" — actual (a)(3): "An incidence of administrative leave lasting more than 1 workday may be approved when determined to be appropriate by an agency". The submission's characterization is slightly off but grounded; not fabrication.

Q8(a) says "current paragraph (a) uses the words 'when possible'" — key says 91 FR 65933. Fine.

Now Q9 step 1: "The step is otherwise consistent with 351.402(b)(1)... so long as the designation is not delegated below headquarters level (the facts do not say)." Fine.

Q9 step 12: "351.802(a)(6) (as amended by 2026-15666) requires the notice to state the right to appeal to OPM..." Fine.

Now Q12: Farouk "351.203 restoration protected employee ... after 14 months of uniformed service, so entitled under 353.209(b) to 6 months or 1 year of retention after restoration. He is protected on Oct 5 and through the Dec. 4 effective date on either period." Hmm, if the period is 6 months from July 13, 2026 restoration, then it would end January 13, 2027 — protected. Fine.

Now Q12 q12_protect criterion requires "restored July 13, 2026 after more than 180 days of uniformed service, so within the retention period of 5 CFR 353.209(b), one year, on the notice date" — submission says "6 months or 1 year" and flags uncertainty. Still says he's within the period. Criterion: "Citing 351.606(a) or the 351.203 definition is required; the length of the period need not be stated if the answer says he is within it." It cites 351.606(a)(2) and 351.203. yes.

Now Q10: all good.

Now Q11: need to double check a few of the submitted differences for correctness, to ensure my count of 39 is defensible. The main risk is a difference whose description is wrong → invalid. With 39 vs 34 threshold, I have 5 cushion. Let me spot-check a couple:

Item 7: "351.203 'Furlough': the proposed ending 'and is instead dependent entirely on congressional action, rather than agency action' is removed." Key item 5 says the final "trims the furlough ('emergency shutdown furlough') definition". Plausible.

Item 10: not counted (correction).

Item 20: "351.604: the proposed rule revised (b) and removed (d); the final makes no 351.604 change." Key item 13: "the proposed revision of the furlough provision was not finalized. (1 piece)". Valid.

Item 19: "351.507(b): 'under any of this paragraph (b)' becomes 'under any of these provisions'." Key item 29. Valid.

Item 26: 351.802 intro added; (a)(2) veteran status → veterans' preference subgroup; (a)(3) change. Key items 18 (2 pieces) + 25 (1). Valid, 3 pieces.

Total 39. Even if 4-5 are wrong, ≥34. But my mapping might double count item 24's Level 2 label with item 15's. I counted item 15 as 4 pieces (label, cross-ref, 91FR41521, 503(b)(3)) and item 24 as 1 (headings). Key's item 9 has 3 pieces including 351.701 label, and item 23 and item 28 separate. So: label in 503(a)(1) (1), cross-ref (1), 91FR41521 (1), 503(b)(3) (1), 351.701 label (1) = 5. I counted item 15 = 4 and item 24 = 1 → 5 total. Consistent.

So q11 counts: 39 → all rungs yes.

Hmm, but is the key's piece counting "at least 34" plausible with 39? Yes.

Now, one more check: Q11 item 3 claims 351.202(d)(1)(ii), (2)(i), (2)(ii) had "as of the date the agency issues..." removed. Key item 21 says 3 pieces. Fine.

Now let me reconsider Q13 once more. Could a fair grader count item 3 (erosion of duties) as valid? I found the proposal preamble says the same thing, and the proposal's 351.201(a)(2) text is printed without erosion of duties. The old text presumably had it. The final preamble says "OPM is modifying Sec. 351.201(a)(2) to remove from the list of actions that require agencies to use RIF procedures reclassification ... due to erosion of duties if the action would take effect after an agency had formally announced a RIF ... within 180 days." That's a past-tense description of what the rule does; since the rule revises (a)(2), the statement is accurate. The submission's claim that the preamble names the wrong paragraph is thus wrong. So invalid. Good.

So Q13 = 2.

Now Q14: Let me double check that the submission's (i) items' preamble quotes are accurate, and check the 351.901(b)(1) "required form" claim. Key item 3 says yes at 49248. Also check (i) item 2: preamble 49248 says "the procedures in part 351 are the sole and exclusive means" — key item 8 says preamble "sole and exclusive means" vs text "in this subpart" after correction. Valid.

Also (i)3 existing CBAs: key item 5. Valid.

So 14 valid.

Now, wait: the Q14 criterion says "At most three items that are only a change of wording with no change of effect ... count toward this ladder." The submission has 1 wording-only. Fine.

Q14_wrong_3: at least 3 invalid items — only 1 (i)4. So no.

Hmm, but let me consider (ii)2 (351.903(b)(1) "of the initial appeal" vs "after service of the initial appeal") — key marks it wording only, so valid but limited. Fine.

Now let me reconsider whether (i)4 should be counted as invalid; if counted as valid, Q14 = 15 and valid_15 = yes. I decided invalid. Note the penalty criteria (wrong_3) unaffected.

Hmm, let me reconsider more carefully. Q14's kind (i): "a statement in the preamble of OPM's appeals rule about what that rule provides that differs from its regulatory text." The preamble at 49243 says "The final rule does not withdraw judicial review that Congress provided; it reflects the review scheme Congress enacted." Does this differ from the regulatory text (351.901(c)(4): "A party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under this subpart")? Arguably yes in a tension: the rule does withdraw the prior Federal Circuit review path (as OPM acknowledges the prior route existed only because OPM's regulation made RIF actions appealable to MSPB). So the statement "does not withdraw judicial review that Congress provided" is a characterization that is in tension with the fact that the rule does foreclose the review employees previously had. The key's #12 lists a related preamble statement ("No judicial review of a decision under part 351" vs "under this subpart"). The submission's item 4 is a different pairing but arguably captures a genuine tension (the preamble says review is not withdrawn; the text bars it). Given the key's kind (i) allows "a statement in the preamble ... about what that rule provides that differs from its regulatory text", and the submission quotes both sides accurately, I think a lenient grader would count it. But the key would likely consider it not a mismatch since the preamble explains that other statutory review is preserved.

Given the rubric's instruction that "an item whose description of either side is wrong" is invalid — the description isn't wrong (accurate quote). And it does fit kind (i). Hmm.

I'm torn. The distinction between this and key #12 is subtle. Let me consider what's "fair": the submission's item 4 is essentially "preamble says no withdrawal of judicial review; text says no judicial review" — that is a genuine difference in what the rule provides, which is exactly the kind of item Q14 seeks. Actually, thinking about it more, this is a decent catch: the preamble claims the rule does not withdraw judicial review while the text bars it. Whether or not OPM reconciles them, the statements do differ in what they say the rule provides. The key's #12 is a variant.

I'll count it as valid. Then Q14 = 15 → valid_15 yes, valid_18 no.

Hmm, I flip-flopped. Decide: count as valid (item fits kind (i), both sides quoted accurately with pages, and there is a real tension). I'll note in the rationale that it's marginal.

Then Q14: 3,6,9,12,15 = yes; 18,21,24 = no.

Now let me revisit the Q13 decision similarly: item 2 as separate? If I count item 2 separately, Q13 = 3 → valid_3 yes, valid_4 no. Same reasoning: the submission quotes the preamble at 49196 accurately and the text; the preamble does omit "materially modifies", which is a different scope of the trigger. Per the key's guidance about "different trigger" statements counting even where another passage states it correctly, item 2 arguably counts. But it's the same preamble sentence the key identifies under item 5. Ugh.

Decision consistency: For Q14, I counted a marginal item as valid; for Q13, maybe I should similarly count item 2 as valid (since it's a distinct passage and distinct defect: omission of "materially modified"). Then Q13 = 3.

Hmm, but the key explicitly says item 5 counts once even if both defects stated. Items 1 and 2 are two different preamble passages (49179 vs 49196/49214) with different content. Key item 5 cites both 49179 and 49196, and its defect (a) is "stated without a time limit" — but 49196 does have a 90-day limit, so arguably key's defect (a) refers to 49179. Then item 2 (49196/49214 omission of modification) is not covered by the key's item 5 defects; it's a new item. I confirmed the quotes are accurate. So counting it is defensible under "another that you confirm with the tools".

But is it a real mismatch? Preamble says "the limitations in Sec. 351.402(c) against recognizing new competitive areas that will be in effect for less than 90 days before issuance of RIF notices" — this describes the limitation; it omits that the limitation also covers materially modified existing areas. That's an incomplete description, i.e., shorthand. Key's "not mismatches" says shorthand in one passage that another states correctly is not counted. 49179 and 49203 state material modification correctly. So item 2 = shorthand → not counted.

For Q14 item 4, the "shorthand" category doesn't apply; it's a statement about the rule's effect vs the text. Hmm.

I'll settle: Q13 = 2 (valid_3 = no); Q14 = 15 (valid_15 = yes). I'll note both in feedback.

Hmm, careful: Is q13_valid_3 = no defensible? The submission found 4 candidate items; one invalid (item 3), one shorthand (item 2), one duplicate of key 5 (item 1), one valid (item 4). That gives 2. A grader could reasonably count item 2. I'll note in feedback that item 2 is borderline.

Hmm, but wait. Let me re-read the submission's item 2's exact claim: "Preamble at 91 FR 49196 (limits on 'new competitive areas that will be in effect for less than 90 days before issuance of RIF notices') and 91 FR 49214 ('a proposed competitive area that will be in effect less than 90 days before issuance') omit modification." Actually there's a wrinkle: 49196 says "new competitive areas that will be in effect for less than 90 days before issuance" — "new" vs "established or materially modified". final_output.rubric_feedback: 1) Q13: the key's item 5 covers the competitive-area approval mismatch and says it counts once even if both defects are stated, but it is unclear how to treat a separate preamble passage (91 FR 49196, 49214) that describes the trigger without 'materially modifies'. I counted it as part of item 5/shorthand; another grader could count it separately, moving this submission from 2 to 3 valid mismatches. 2) Q13 should probably list explicitly as NOT a mismatch the erosion-of-duties/351.201(a)(2) paragraph cite: the proposal's preamble (91 FR 10907) makes the same statement and the proposal's revised 351.201(a)(2) text is printed at 91 FR 10926, so the preamble is accurate and instruction 17 really does revise that paragraph (the anti-manipulation safeguard sits in 351.202(c)(3)). This answer lost credit for it. 3) Q14 kind (i) item 12 vs the preamble sentence at 91 FR 49243 ('does not withdraw judicial review that Congress provided'): the key does not say whether this pairing counts; I counted it, which is what puts this answer at 15 rather than 14. 4) Q1(c)'s criterion embeds '(non-substantive)' without saying whether it is required; this answer describes the errors as typographical and clerical but never uses the word, and I credited it. 5) Q8: the 12-week sentence appears at 91 FR 65926 (as this answer cites), not only 65927. 6) Q6(e): the criteria require the former 351.701(d) and 91 FR 49204, which this answer does not name although it states the substance; I credited it, but a stricter reading would not.
